answer: One concrete defense bonds each agent to a costly, non-transferable work history, so spawning a new identity means rebuilding reputation from zero. When a peer vouches, trust only ripples outward as far as that peer's own stake can cover, capping how far a cheap fake spreads. A sybil swarm then resembles footprints scattered over a shifting dune: countless yet weightless, each quickly erased. Honest agents instead accrue a deep umber patina of attested work — an aged record no duplicate can cheaply forge.
